title: Static pods that reference ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs or ServiceAccounts are rejected by the kubelet

detection.reason: the projection carries env API references (hasEnvApiRefs) but a volume or serviceAccountName reference is not reducible to one predicate; a false CLEARED on a control-plane pod is worse than a hint

quote: Static pods that reference API objects were denied admission by the kubelet so that static pods would not be silently running even after the mirror pod creation failed.
remediation: A static pod manifest (under the kubelet's staticPodPath) whose env, envFrom, volumes or serviceAccountName reference an API object stops being admitted after the kubelet upgrade and the pod does not run. Inline the values (hostPath, literal env) before upgrading the node. The gate `PreventStaticPodAPIReferences` can be disabled on the kubelet as a temporary fallback.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["kubernetes.io/config.mirror"] != null) | select((.spec.serviceAccountName != null and .spec.serviceAccountName != "default") or ([.spec.volumes[]? | select(.configMap or .secret or .persistentVolumeClaim or .projected)] | length != 0) or ([.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.valueFrom.configMapKeyRef or .valueFrom.secretKeyRef)] | length != 0) or ([.spec.containers[].envFrom[]?] | length != 0)) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # every static pod listed is denied by a 1.34 kubelet

title: Out-of-tree kube-scheduler plugins must be rebuilt for the 1.34 framework (PreFilter takes NodeInfos)

detection.reason: whether a custom scheduler binary is in use is not visible in the inventory

quote: The PreFilter plugins now accepted the `NodeInfo` list from the arguments.
remediation: Only clusters running a custom-built kube-scheduler with out-of-tree PreFilter plugins are affected; rebuild against the 1.34 framework before rolling the control plane.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[*].image}{"\n"}{end}'  # an image other than registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler is a custom build

title: Nodes labelled node.kubernetes.io/exclude-from-external-load-balancers=false are now INCLUDED in cloud load balancers

detection.reason: the detection needs the label's VALUE; the evaluator matches label keys only, so the hint names every node carrying the key and the command prints the value

remediation: Until 1.34 any value of the label excluded the node; from 1.34 only a non-`false` value does. Nodes carrying `=false` (often control-plane nodes copied from a template) become load-balancer backends after the cloud-controller-manager upgrade — remove the label or set it to `true` where exclusion was intended.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodes -L node.kubernetes.io/exclude-from-external-load-balancers --no-headers | awk '$NF == "false"'  # each node printed becomes an external LB backend at 1.34

title: DRA admin-access namespace label renamed to resource.kubernetes.io/admin-access
quote: the alpha-level `resource.k8s.io/admin-access` label has been updated to `resource.kubernetes.io/admin-access`. Admins using the alpha feature and updating from 1.33 can set both labels, upgrade, then remove `resource.k8s.io/admin-access`
remediation: Add `resource.kubernetes.io/admin-access: "true"` next to the old label on every namespace that holds adminAccess claims BEFORE upgrading; claims in a namespace with only the old label are rejected by 1.34.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ns -l resource.k8s.io/admin-access -L resource.kubernetes.io/admin-access  # rows with an empty last column need the new label before the upgrade

title: DRA scheduling: Filter now times out after 10s (configurable via FilterTimeout)

detection.reason: filter runtime is a scheduler-side measurement; pods that reference claims mark the clusters that care

quote: The scheduler plugin prevented abnormal filter runtimes by timing out after 10 seconds. This was configurable via the plugin configuration's `FilterTimeout`. Setting it to zero disabled the timeout and restored the behavior of Kubernetes <= 1.33.
remediation: Large clusters with complex claims that previously took longer than 10s to place a pod now see the pod stay Pending with a timeout reason; raise `FilterTimeout` in the DynamicResources plugin config or simplify the claim.
verifyCommand: kubectl get events -A --field-selector reason=FailedScheduling -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.message | test("timed out")) | .involvedObject.namespace + "/" + .involvedObject.name + ": " + .message'  # after the upgrade, DRA filter timeouts show up here

title: DRA drivers speaking the v1alpha4 kubelet gRPC API stop working on 1.34 kubelets

detection.reason: the gRPC version a driver speaks is not visible in its DaemonSet; pods that reference claims mark the clusters that care

quote: removed support for the v1alpha4 kubelet gRPC API (added in 1.31, superseded in 1.32). DRA drivers using the helper package from Kubernetes >= 1.32 use the v1beta1 API and continue to be supported.
remediation: Upgrade every DRA driver to a release built on the 1.32+ `kubeletplugin` helper (v1beta1, or v1 from 1.34) before upgrading the nodes; a v1alpha4-only driver is not registered and its devices vanish from the node.
verifyCommand: kubectl get resourceslices -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.driver' | sort -u  # every driver listed must be built on the 1.32-or-newer kubeletplugin helper
coversNotes: DRA kubelet: gRPC API graduated to v1, v1beta1 was deprecated starting in 1.34. Updating

title: Downward API resourceFieldRef limits now fall back to pod-level limits before node allocatable

detection.reason: needs a pod-level limit AND a resourceFieldRef AND no container limit on one pod; not one predicate

quote: if container-level limits were not set, pod-level limits were now used before falling back to node allocatable resources.
remediation: A container in a pod that sets `spec.resources` limits and reads `limits.cpu` / `limits.memory` through the Downward API without its own limits sees the pod value instead of the node capacity after the upgrade; check JVM/GOMAXPROCS-style sizing that consumed the old value.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.resources.limits != null) | select(any(.spec.containers[]; .resources.limits == null and any(.env[]?; .valueFrom.resourceFieldRef != null))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # these pods read a different value after 1.34

title: kubeadm-managed etcd moves to 3.6 — the 3.5 members must be healthy and on the v3.5 storage format first

detection.reason: the etcd binary version and store format are not collected; the static etcd pod's image is the nearest signal

remediation: Before `kubeadm upgrade apply` to 1.34, confirm every etcd member runs 3.5.x with `etcdctl endpoint status` and that no member still carries a 3.4-format store; etcd 3.6 refuses to start from an older on-disk format and the control plane stays down. Take an etcd snapshot first. Externally managed etcd is unaffected.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=etcd -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}'  # kubeadm-managed members that kubeadm will move to 3.6

title: AppArmor profiles set in securityContext are no longer mirrored into the beta annotations
quote: `AppArmor` profiles specified in the Pod or container `SecurityContext` were no longer copied to deprecated `AppArmor` annotations (prefix `container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/`). Anything that inspected the deprecated annotations must be migrated to use the `SecurityContext` fields instead.
remediation: Admission policies, Gatekeeper/Kyverno constraints, and monitoring that read `container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/<container>` stop seeing profiles for pods that set them via `securityContext.appArmorProfile`. Move those consumers to the fields; move manifests that still SET the annotation to the fields as well.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations | keys[]? | startswith("container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' | sort -u  # pods still on the annotation path; new pods created from fields will not carry it

title: topologySpreadConstraints.matchLabelKeys is now merged into labelSelector by the API server — a 1.32→1.34 skip upgrade changes spreading
quote: The Kubernetes API server merged selectors built from `matchLabelKeys` into the `labelSelector` of `topologySpreadConstraints`, aligning Pod Topology Spread behavior with Inter-Pod Affinity.
remediation: Pods created on a 1.34 API server carry the merged selector in `labelSelector`; the scheduler's compatibility path that honoured `matchLabelKeys` on older pods ends here. Upgrading straight from 1.32 to 1.34 (skipping 1.33) leaves pods whose selector was never merged and whose spreading the 1.34 scheduler no longer corrects — roll those workloads after the upgrade. Controllers that read `labelSelector` back (e.g. to build their own selectors) must expect the extra `In` requirements.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.topologySpreadConstraints[]?; .matchLabelKeys != null)) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # pods spread by matchLabelKeys; the selector merge applies to them on recreation

title: kube-scheduler no longer clears status.nominatedNodeName — autoscalers and custom schedulers own the field

detection.reason: which external component manages nominatedNodeName is not a collected object

quote: The scheduler no longer cleared the `nominatedNodeName` field for Pods. External components, such as Cluster Autoscaler and Karpenter, were responsible for managing this field when needed.
remediation: A stale `nominatedNodeName` (the node was deleted or the preemption abandoned) stays on the pod until something else clears it; check the Cluster Autoscaler / Karpenter release in use handles it (both do from their 1.34-compatible releases) and that dashboards do not read the field as live intent.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.nominatedNodeName != null and .spec.nodeName == null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " nominated=" + .status.nominatedNodeName'  # pending pods carrying a nomination; after 1.34 only an external component clears a stale one
coversNotes: The scheduler no longer clears the `nominatedNodeName` field for Pods. External
